To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the pressure drop in a mushy zone depends on the grain size distribution and the liquid film thickness.
the transition from continuous films to a coherent structure occurs when the liquid fraction reaches 0.5 and is associated with a sharp increase of the pressure drop.

the pressure drop is a strong function of the grain diameter and the solid fraction, that it increases with the grain diameter, and that it is higher for a granular model than for an average pressure drop model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transition of the mushy region from a state of continuous liquid films to the formation of a coherent solid.
the transition of the mushy region from a continuous liquid films to an interconnected network of liquid films.
the transition from continuous films of liquid to a coherent solid, and the associated loss of feeding ability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transition of the mushy region from continuous liquid films (or films with some discontinuities) to a coherent solid (or solid with some liquid inclusions) is a gradual process which is strongly dependent on the grain size and the solidification rate, and that it is not an instantaneous phenomenon.
the transition from liquid films to a connected solid network is a very complex phenomenon that involves a large number of parameters.
the transition from continuous to discontinuous liquid films in a mushy zone is not a simple percolation phenomenon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transition to a coherent mushy zone can be characterized by a critical value of the solid volume fraction.
the coalescence of equiaxed dendrites leads to a percolation threshold, which is the transition from a continuous liquid film to a coherent solid.
the transition of the mushy region from continuous liquid films (percolation) to coherent solid (percolation of solid grains) is a key issue in solidification.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a more realistic description of the liquid feeding ability of the mushy can be obtained by taking into account both the pressure loss associated with the coherency development and the solidification shrinkage.
the coalescence of liquid films is a crucial step in the transition from continuous films to coherent solid.
the pressure drop in a mushy zone with a low volume fraction of solid is not only a function of the solid volume fraction, but also of the connectivity of the solid skeleton.
